title: Carolingian Empire
capsule: Between 718 and 724, Charles Martel, illegitimate son of Pepin of Herstal, completed his rise from fugitive challenger to sole mayor of the palace over both Austrasia and Neustria, ruling in the name of the Merovingian kings Chlothar IV, Chilperic II and, from 721, Theuderic IV. Having broken his rivals at Amblève (716) and Vincy (717), he pacified Neustria at the Battle of Soissons (718-719), forced the Frisian king Redbad's forces back from the lower Rhine after Redbad's death in 719, and campaigned against the Saxons along the Weser. These years mark the effective founding of Carolingian power nearly a century before the dynasty's imperial coronation of 800, as Charles's family displaced the Merovingians as Francia's true rulers in all but name.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core Frankish territories in Gaul and the Rhineland are well attested by royal diplomas, capitularies, and ecclesiastical records from the sixth century onward; the extent of tributary or nominal Frankish authority over peripheral peoples such as Bretons and Basques is less precisely bounded. Capsule researched for this polity/era specifically (confidence: high).
